claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: Write D={d_1<...<d_k}. All marks are determined before movement. Moving p_{d_1},...,p_{d_k} successively to the front leaves them in order p_{d_k},...,p_{d_1}; removing them never changes the relative order of the unmarked elements. This proves the displayed formula exactly.
claims.search_method: Direct operational proof, followed by exhaustive comparison of the closed formula with a separate literal mark-then-MoveToFront implementation on every permutation of sizes 1 through 9.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: Element i is unmarked because every active predecessor is smaller. The first element of R is marked because it follows i, while r_j for j>=2 remains to the right of i exactly when r_{j-1}<r_j. Moves originating in L cannot end to the right of i, and the fixed increasing suffix remains untouched. Thus the new right word is exactly A(R); induction gives A^t(R), and i is fixed exactly when this word is empty.
claims.search_method: Symbolic one-round analysis and induction; additionally checked every applicable fixed-suffix phase in every permutation of sizes 1 through 9 and compared literal A iteration with the monotone-stack extinction computation.

claims.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case number of nontrivial rounds, then W(n)<=n(n-1)/2. Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: At any unsorted state, choose the largest unfixed value i. All larger values form a permanent fixed suffix. Claim 1 makes its phase length h(R); since A omits the first entry on every nonempty iteration, h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. These successive phases are disjoint, with zero length for values already fixed, so W(n)<=sum_{i=2}^n(i-1)=n(n-1)/2. Dividing by n^2 immediately excludes little-omega(n^2).
claims.search_method: General phase decomposition proof, supplemented by exhaustive verification of the bound for all permutations through n=9.

claims.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
claims.evidence: Define B_0 empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). Claim 0 gives by induction T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1, so n first becomes fixed after n-1 rounds. For m=n-1, label a decreasing monotone stack by assigning each new x one plus the maximum label among smaller popped entries; induction on A-iterations shows these are deletion rounds. Writing m=q(q+1)/2+r with 0<=r<=q, the B_m recurrence gives stack labels (1,q,q-1,...,q-r,q-r-2,...,1) when r<=q-2 and (1,q,q-1,...,1) when r is q-1 or q, so its maximum is q. Since B_m=mR with R=T(B_{m-1}), A(B_m)=A(R), hence h(R)=q. The exact inequalities q(q+1)<=2m<(q+1)(q+2) identify q with the stated floor and prove the lower bound.
claims.witness: The family p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1); complete exact trajectories were instantiated for every 3<=n<=100.
claims.search_method: Induction on the special trajectory and labeled monotone-stack invariant; exact integer checks used isqrt and triangular inequalities, verified the full labeled invariant through m=1000, and used no floating-point decisions.

claims.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
claims.evidence: The checker enumerated all sum_{n=1}^9 n!=409113 permutations. It first compared the closed round formula against an independently implemented literal marking queue and sequential MoveToFront operation for every state, then iterated transformations with cycle detection and took each exact maximum. The resulting maxima were exactly 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
claims.witness: For n=1 use (1); for 2<=n<=8, (n,1,2,...,n-1) attains the stated maximum; for n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) takes 26 rounds.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of every permutation for each 1<=n<=9 using exact integer comparisons and two independently coded one-round semantics.

target_evidence: The target asks for an asymptotically tight worst-case round count and, in particular, an answer to whether omega(n^2) rounds are possible. The verified quadratic upper bound settles that explicit subquestion negatively. However, the proved family lower bound remains only linear and the finite values through n=9 do not provide a matching asymptotic lower bound, so the tight order is still undetermined. The final writeup expressly acknowledges this gap and labels the resolution PARTIAL; that coverage assessment is accurate and not overclaimed.
